title: Stop the chicken-walk assertion failing at random in CI
tier_reason: a timing tolerance in a test; nothing about the game changes
ask: tools/test_runner.gd's assertion "she walks while the game is running" (the chicken entity, around line 752) failed once and passed on an immediate re-run on 2026-09-07, with no related change in the diff. It waits a fixed 20 process frames for the chicken's sprite to move after its registry position is set, which is a wall-clock assumption on a machine that may be loaded. Replace the frame count with the file's own `_wait_until` helper and a generous timeout, the way the door and teaching scenarios already do, so a slow frame is not a failure. Check the file for other fixed-frame waits with the same shape while you are there.
first_action: Reproduce by running the integration suite under load, then swap the fixed frame count for _wait_until.
why: Daniel's standing rule is that a red suite must mean something is broken, not that bookkeeping is pending — a test that fails at random teaches the team to ignore red.
